car.body_description: American 3D-printed hybrid hypercar with a distinctive 1+1 tandem cockpit (driver centered, passenger directly behind — NOT side-by-side), teardrop single canopy tapering sharply toward the rear, exposed raw 3D-printed structural lattice panels at the rear diffuser and rear suspension area, conventional dark carbon fiber front splitter, quad central exhausts, aggressive active rear wing, slit-style narrow front lights, very low and wide Le Mans prototype-like silhouette.

signature_detail.element: quad central exhaust cluster with 3D-printed lattice diffuser surround
signature_detail.location: rear center, below the rear deck and between the rear haunches
signature_detail.why: The four tightly-packed exhaust tips surrounded by organic 3D-printed lattice diffuser structure is the Czinger's most visually striking and unique rear detail — more photogenic than the subtle 'C' badge. No other car has this combination of quad exhausts nested in topology-optimized lattice.
signature_detail.visual_description: Four circular polished metal exhaust tips arranged in a tight 2x2 cluster at the center of the rear diffuser, surrounded by raw matte charcoal 3D-printed lattice struts that branch organically around them like a skeletal cage. Wine oxblood pearl rear body curves frame the cluster from above and both sides. The active rear wing's underside and trailing edge sweep across the top of the frame.
signature_detail.camera_approach: low behind the car at 6 o'clock, looking slightly upward into the diffuser area, so the exhaust tips catch studio light as bright metallic circles against the dark lattice

paint.name: deep wine oxblood pearl
paint.description: Deep wine oxblood pearl paint across all body panels — dark burgundy red with subtle dark-metallic flake catching the studio lights, NOT bright red, NOT maroon-brown, NOT pink
paint.lattice_treatment: Raw 3D-printed lattice panels (REAR ONLY — at the rear diffuser and rear suspension area) stay unpainted matte charcoal. The front of the car has a conventional dark carbon fiber splitter, NOT exposed lattice. Do not add lattice to the front of the car.
paint.wheels: Polished gunmetal multi-spoke forged wheels, same spoke count and finish across all shots
paint.calipers: Red brake calipers visible behind the wheel spokes

studio.description: Infinite seamless mid-grey (#6a6a6a) cyclorama, evenly lit edge to edge and top to bottom with a subtle soft gradient from slightly darker upper area to slightly brighter mid area behind the car, then flat grey floor curving up into the wall with no visible seam, bright clean even studio lighting like high-end Pagani, Koenigsegg, or Porsche press photography

shots.composition_notes: Wide full-car shot. The car's nose points toward camera-left, the right flank recedes to the right. Entire car visible from front splitter to rear wing. Headlights on with subtle warm glow. Wine paint catches cool rim light along the right fender peak. Small soft floor reflection directly beneath the car only.

shots.shot_name: pure side profile showing the LEFT flank
shots.camera_clock: 9 o'clock (directly to the left of the car)
shots.composition_notes: Complete left flank of the car visible — left front wheel on the viewer's left, left door in the middle, left rear wheel on the viewer's right. Teardrop tandem canopy silhouette clearly readable against the grey backdrop. Active rear wing visible at upper-right of silhouette. Front splitter lattice at lower-left. Diffuser with 3D-printed lattice at lower-right.

shots.shot_name: tight rear close-up — quad exhaust cluster hero with lattice diffuser surround
shots.camera_clock: 6 o'clock low (directly behind the car, looking slightly upward into the diffuser and exhaust area)
shots.composition_notes: Tight rear close-up in the style of the wine Ferrari shot3 reference — abstract, sexy, but still instantly identifiable as the rear of a hypercar. NOT the full car, NOT a wide shot, but NOT an extreme unrecognizable macro either. The HERO element is the quad central exhaust cluster: four circular polished metal exhaust tips arranged in a tight 2x2 cluster, glinting with studio light as bright metallic circles against the surrounding dark lattice. The 3D-printed lattice diffuser struts branch organically around the exhaust tips like a skeletal cage — raw matte charcoal against the polished metal tips. Three orientation anchors: (1) top ~25% of frame shows the underside of the active rear wing sweeping dramatically across as a dark carbon curve, with a sliver of wine oxblood pearl rear deck paint visible between the wing and the body — this signals REAR OF CAR, (2) middle ~45% of frame shows the quad exhaust tips (hero, razor-sharp) nested in the 3D-printed lattice diffuser cage, (3) bottom ~30% of frame shows the lower diffuser edge and a subtle floor reflection, with wine rear haunch curves framing the cluster from both sides at the left and right edges. Rear taillight signatures visible as small glowing red accents at the far left and right edges. Moderate DOF f/5.6 — exhaust tips and surrounding lattice in razor focus, wing edge and body curves slightly soft but clearly readable. Wine paint catches subtle rim light on the haunch curves. Grey studio visible around the edges.

shots.shot_name: rear 3/4 right low hero (longest dwell shot)
shots.composition_notes: Crouched low almost ground level, looking slightly up at the rear wing. Rear end dominates the frame — active rear wing raised prominently on its central pylon at the top, quad central exhaust outlets in the diffuser center, wide rear haunches curving outward on both sides, exposed 3D-printed lattice panels clearly visible in the diffuser structure between the exhausts. Right rear wheel visible at bottom-right (must match shot1 wheel design exactly). Car's nose recedes into the upper-left of the frame with front-left fender and headlight visible at small scale giving a sense of the car's length. Cool rim light tracing the rear wing trailing edge.

shots.shot_name: front-right wheel and brake caliper detail
shots.camera_clock: ground level beside the front-right tire at 2-3 o'clock, looking slightly inward and upward
shots.composition_notes: Tight-but-readable crop of the front-right wheel from shot1 — NOT extreme macro. Viewer must immediately recognize 'that's the front wheel of the same hypercar' within 0.5 seconds. Three orientation anchors must be visible: (1) top-left corner shows a small glimpse of the slit-style front-right headlight with subtle warm glow (signals FRONT of car), (2) top ~25% of frame shows the wine oxblood pearl front-right fender curving outward and downward around the wheel well, catching soft rim light along the peak, (3) middle and bottom ~65% of frame shows the gunmetal multi-spoke forged wheel with the red brake caliper clearly visible in the caliper window between spokes, front spoke faces in razor focus, tire sidewall and contact patch visible at the bottom. Bottom-left corner shows a small glimpse of the charcoal 3D-printed front splitter lattice (signals CZINGER specifically). Moderate DOF f/5.6 — spokes and caliper razor sharp, fender and tire slightly soft but clearly readable.

shots.shot_name: angled front headlight and nose detail from 1-2 o'clock low
shots.camera_clock: 1-2 o'clock low (front-right of the car, crouched beside the front corner, looking across the nose at an angle)
shots.composition_notes: Angled front detail — camera is OFF-CENTER at roughly 1-2 o'clock, crouched low beside the front-right corner, shooting across the nose. NOT a symmetric dead-front crop (that is shot 8). IMPORTANT: this is a REALISTIC close-up of a real car's front end — all proportions must be physically accurate to the real Czinger 21C. Do NOT exaggerate, enlarge, or invent any body elements. The front of the Czinger 21C has smooth wine-painted bodywork with a conventional carbon fiber front splitter (NOT a massive exposed lattice — the lattice is only at the REAR of the car). Three orientation anchors: (1) the right-side slit headlight is the HERO element — a narrow aggressive LED light signature viewed at an angle, glowing warm, clearly the front headlight of a hypercar, filling the upper-left ~30% of the frame, (2) middle ~40% shows the smooth wine oxblood pearl front nose, fender, and hood curving away from camera toward the left, Czinger badge visible on the hood at an angle, wine paint catching a strong rim light highlight along the right fender peak — smooth bodywork with realistic panel gaps and air intake vents, (3) bottom ~30% shows the dark carbon fiber front splitter (conventional flat carbon, NOT a giant lattice cage) and a glimpse of the front-right tire and gunmetal wheel at the bottom-right corner. Moderate DOF f/5.6 — headlight and nearest fender in razor focus, far side of hood falls into gentle bokeh. Grey studio visible at the left edge.

Mirror image of shot 1's pose. The car's nose points toward camera-right, the LEFT flank recedes to the left. Viewer sees the front grille area, the LEFT headlight (slit-style, lit with warm glow), the LEFT front fender, the LEFT wing mirror with a small shadow cast on the left door, the LEFT door with its body lines, and the LEFT front wheel at the bottom. The right side of the car is hidden behind the body. Wine paint catches cool rim light along the LEFT fender peak. Lighting setup stays fixed to the studio (not the car), so the key light direction on the body appears mirrored from shot 1 — this is intentional and physically correct; the camera moved but the studio lights stayed put.

shots.camera_clock: 12 o'clock (directly in front of the car on the exact centerline)
shots.composition_notes: Perfectly bilaterally symmetric hero — left and right halves of the frame mirror each other pixel-wise. Both headlights lit with subtle warm glow. Czinger badge centered at the top of the hood. Front splitter 3D-printed lattice visible at the bottom center. Both front fenders curving outward symmetrically. Both front wheels visible at the bottom corners with gunmetal spokes and red calipers peeking through. Teardrop tandem canopy silhouette rising behind the front clip, centered. Active rear wing barely visible peeking over the roof at the top center.
